title: The Sunday Read: ‘Chronic Pain Is a Hidden Epidemic. It’s Time for a Revolution.’

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空漫步七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.zh: 今天我在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.

sentences.en: I used to think of pain as something that you got over.
sentences.zh: 我过去认为疼痛是那种你熬一熬就能过去的。

sentences.en: I did a lot of sports for most of my life and so I've sprained my ankle pretty badly.
sentences.zh: 我大半辈子都在做很多运动，所以我曾把脚踝扭得很重。

sentences.en: I dislocated a shoulder, broke my hand.
sentences.zh: 我脱臼过肩膀，摔断过手。

sentences.en: Sometimes it hurt for weeks or for months.
sentences.zh: 有时候它会疼上几周或几个月。

sentences.en: But, you know, I would take some Advil or do some physical therapy and eventually the pain would go away.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，我会吃点止痛药或者做点物理治疗，最终疼痛就会消失。

sentences.en: Until one day, a couple of years ago, it didn't.
sentences.zh: 直到几年前的某一天，它没有消失。

sentences.en: My name's Jennifer Kahn and I am a contributing writer for the New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫詹妮弗·卡恩，我是《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: I write about the complex ways that science and new technologies affect people.
sentences.zh: 我撰写关于科学和新技术如何以复杂方式影响人们的文章。

sentences.en: And in the past, those stories weren't personal.
sentences.zh: 在过去，那些故事与我无关。

sentences.en: This time was a little different.
sentences.zh: 这次有点不一样。

sentences.en: I was shocked to learn that until recently, it had been more than 20 years since a new pain drug was approved.
sentences.zh: 我震惊地发现，直到最近，距离上一款新止痛药获批已经过去20多年了。

sentences.en: At least one that was not an opioid.
sentences.zh: 至少是指那种不是阿片类药物的药。

sentences.en: And I learned this because I developed chronic pain myself.
sentences.zh: 我了解到这一点是因为我自己也患上了慢性疼痛。

sentences.en: Once I did, I realized there are so many people out there who are in the same position.
sentences.zh: 一旦我有了这种经历，我意识到有那么多人和我处在同样的境地。

sentences.en: And for those people, pain is with them all the time.
sentences.zh: 对于那些人来说，疼痛时刻伴随着他们。

sentences.en: And it makes it difficult to do almost anything.
sentences.zh: 这使得几乎做什么事都变得困难。

sentences.en: To work, to exercise, to see your friends.
sentences.zh: 工作、锻炼、见朋友。

sentences.en: You know, even just to enjoy life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，甚至只是享受生活。

sentences.en: And learning that sent me on a reporting journey that you'll hear about in this week's Sunday Read.
sentences.zh: 了解到这一点让我踏上了一段采访之旅，你将在本周的《周日阅读》中听到。

sentences.en: As many as one in three Americans have chronic pain or have dealt with it at some point in their lives.
sentences.zh: 多达三分之一的美国人患有慢性疼痛，或者在人生的某个阶段经历过慢性疼痛。

sentences.en: But there are still only a handful of treatment options available.
sentences.zh: 但可供选择的治疗方案仍然只有寥寥几种。

sentences.en: There are opioids, there are anti-inflammatories, certain drugs for nerve pain maybe.
sentences.zh: 有阿片类药物，有抗炎药，也许还有针对神经痛的某些药物。

sentences.en: But not all of them work well.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有药物都管用。

sentences.en: And because there's no way for even an expert to see pain, it's not always taken seriously.
sentences.zh: 而且因为即使是专家也无法看到疼痛，它并不总是被严肃对待。

sentences.en: Even doctors might say to you, well, maybe it's all in your head.
sentences.zh: 甚至医生也可能会对你说，嗯，也许这都是你的幻觉。

sentences.en: Or honestly, it's probably not that bad, right?
sentences.zh: 或者老实说，可能没那么严重吧？

sentences.en: In my case, for instance, I can feel electric sparks in my hands all the time.
sentences.zh: 以我为例，我能一直感觉到手上有电流般的刺痛。

sentences.en: But it's impossible for a medical professional to detect them.
sentences.zh: 但医疗专业人员根本无法检测到它们。

sentences.en: All they can do is ask how I feel on a scale of 1 to 10.
sentences.zh: 他们唯一能做的就是问我从1到10分感觉如何。

sentences.en: But, you know, what does that mean relative to anybody else?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这和其他任何人相比意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: So I started reaching out to experts because I wanted to know how we got here.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始联系专家，因为我想知道我们是如何走到这一步的。

sentences.en: And the more people I talked to, the more I learned that while there's still no silver bullet, there actually is a revolution developing in chronic pain research right now.
sentences.zh: 我交谈的人越多，我就越了解到，虽然现在仍然没有灵丹妙药，但实际上慢性疼痛研究领域正在酝酿一场革命。

sentences.en: What we're seeing in medicine is this combination of actually trying to understand the deep root causes of pain
sentences.zh: 我们在医学上看到的是，一方面努力去理解疼痛的深层根本原因，另一方面又意识到治疗需要更具针对性、更精准、更有效。

sentences.en: and realizing that treatments need to be more targeted and more precise and more effective.
sentences.zh: 另一方面又意识到治疗需要更具针对性、更精准、更有效。

sentences.en: Scientists are also starting to see chronic pain as a disease in its own right, a disease of the nervous system, where it used to be just a black box.
sentences.zh: 科学家们也开始将慢性疼痛视为一种独立的疾病，一种神经系统的疾病，而它过去只是一个黑匣子。

sentences.en: I spoke with Alan Bassbaum, who oversees a pain research lab at the University of California, San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 我采访了艾伦·巴斯鲍姆，他负责加州大学旧金山分校的一个疼痛研究实验室，

sentences.en: and he likened this moment to the breakthroughs we saw in cancer research 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 他把这个时刻比作我们20年前在癌症研究中看到的突破。

sentences.en: Doctors used to treat cancer based on where a tumor was located, like in the liver or the stomach.
sentences.zh: 医生过去常常根据肿瘤所在的位置来治疗癌症，比如在肝脏或胃里。

sentences.en: But once they were able to study tumors at a cellular level, they realized they needed to change their entire approach to treatment.
sentences.zh: 但一旦他们能够在细胞水平上研究肿瘤，他们就意识到必须改变整个治疗方法。

sentences.en: That's the revolution we're seeing in chronic pain right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在在慢性疼痛领域看到的革命。

sentences.en: We're understanding it at a cellular and molecular level to treat it more effectively.
sentences.zh: 我们正在从细胞和分子层面理解它，以便更有效地治疗它。

sentences.en: And the experts I talked to told me that they think we're actually going to see a lot of new treatments, even within the next five years,
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的专家告诉我，他们认为我们实际上会在五年内看到很多新的治疗方法，

sentences.en: which is a stunning timeline for coming up with new drugs.
sentences.zh: 对于研发新药来说，这是一个惊人的时间表。

sentences.en: So here's my story, read by Kirsten Potter.
sentences.zh: 以下是我的故事，由克斯滕·波特朗读。

sentences.en: Our audio producer today is Adrienne HurSt.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的音频制作人是阿德里安娜·赫斯特。

sentences.en: The original music you'll hear was written and performed by Aaron Esposito.
sentences.zh: 你将听到的原创音乐由亚伦·埃斯波西托创作和演奏。

sentences.en: Here's a strange story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个奇怪的故事。

sentences.en: One day, two summers ago, I woke up because my arms, both of them, hurt.
sentences.zh: 两个夏天前的某一天，我醒来时发现我的胳膊，两条胳膊都痛。

sentences.en: Not the way they do when you've slept in a funny position, but as if the tendons in my forearms and hands were moving through mud.
sentences.zh: 不是那种以奇怪的姿势睡觉后感到的酸痛，而是仿佛我前臂和小臂以及手部的肌腱在泥泞中移动一样。

sentences.en: What felt like sharp electric shocks kept sparking in my fingers and sometimes up the inside of my biceps and across my cheSt.
sentences.zh: 感觉像锐利的触电一样不断在我的手指间闪现，有时顺着二头肌内侧一直蔓延到胸口。

sentences.en: Holding anything was excruciating.
sentences.zh: 握住任何东西都是一种折磨。

sentences.en: A cup, a toothbrush, my phone.
sentences.zh: 一个杯子、一把牙刷、我的手机。

sentences.en: Even doing nothing was miserable.
sentences.zh: 甚至什么都不做也很痛苦。

sentences.en: It hurt when I sat with my hands in my lap, when I stood, when I lay flat on the bed or on my side.
sentences.zh: 当我把手放在膝盖上坐着时、当我站着时、当我平躺在床上或侧躺时，都会痛。

sentences.en: The slightest pressure, a bed sheet, a watch band, a bra strap, was intolerable.
sentences.zh: 哪怕是最轻微的压力，比如床单、手表带、胸罩带，都让人无法忍受。

sentences.en: It was August, and every doctor seemed to be away on vacation.
sentences.zh: 那是八月，每个医生似乎都出去度假了。

sentences.en: The ones I did manage to see were politely stumped.
sentences.zh: 我设法见到的那些医生都礼貌地束手无策。

sentences.en: It wasn't carpal tunnel, tennis elbow, or any other injury they could identify.
sentences.zh: 这不是腕管综合征、网球肘，也不是他们能识别的其他任何损伤。

sentences.en: I did nothing unusual the day before.
sentences.zh: 前一天我没有做任何不寻常的事。

sentences.en: An hour of work on my laptop, followed by a visit with a friend.
sentences.zh: 在笔记本电脑上工作了一个小时，接着去拜访了一位朋友。

sentences.en: We sat in her backyard and talked.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在她家的后院聊天。

sentences.en: For the first few weeks, I could barely sleep.
sentences.zh: 最初的几个星期，我几乎无法入睡。

sentences.en: Over the following months, I lost weight, almost a pound a week.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几个月里，我瘦了，几乎每周瘦一磅。

sentences.en: I couldn't drive or cook or use my laptop for work or even hold a book or a pen.
sentences.zh: 我不能开车、做饭、用笔记本电脑工作，甚至连拿一本书或一支笔都做不到。

sentences.en: I would have been bored, except the pain was so tiring that I could barely function.
sentences.zh: 本来我会觉得无聊，但疼痛太累人了，以至于我几乎无法运作。

sentences.en: I spent the days shuffling around the house listening to audiobooks and doing voice-to-text searches for nerve pain, arms, with my phone flat on the table,
sentences.zh: 我白天在屋里拖着步子走来走去，听着有声书，把手机平放在桌上，用语音转文字搜索神经痛、胳膊，

sentences.en: then carefully, painfully scrolling through the results.
sentences.zh: 然后小心翼翼、痛苦地滚动查看搜索结果。

sentences.en: I think we're past the point where I have to explain that chronic pain is not the result of imbalanced humors, or a wandering uterus, or possession by demons.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经不需要再解释慢性疼痛不是体液失衡、子宫游走或恶魔附身的结果了。

sentences.en: But for more modern skeptics, this is where I should add that chronic pain also isn't just all-in-your-head, or not-really-that-bad, or any of the other ways in which people who
sentences.zh: 但对于更现代的怀疑论者，我应该补充一点，慢性疼痛也不是全凭臆想、或者其实没那么严重，或者其他那些让饱受其苦的人

sentences.en: suffer from it are still regularly gaslit and dismissed.
sentences.zh: 经常被精神虐待和驳回的方式。

sentences.en: Personally, I never had to contend with not being believed.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我从来没有遇到过不被相信的情况。

sentences.en: Almost certainly, because I'm an otherwise healthy, reasonably well-off white woman with a clean medical history and no significant record of anxiety or depression.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定，因为我是一个在其他方面健康、相当富裕的白人女性，有着干净的病史，而且没有重大的焦虑或抑郁记录。

sentences.en: Instead, I was taken seriously.
sentences.zh: 相反，我受到了严肃对待。

sentences.en: A whole gamut of tests was run.
sentences.zh: 进行了一整套检查。

sentences.en: My wrists were x-rayed.
sentences.zh: 我的手腕拍了X光片。

sentences.en: I had an MRI on my cervical spine.
sentences.zh: 我对颈椎做了磁共振成像。

sentences.en: Each new doctor ordered new blood tests, some for vitamin deficiencies, others for autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis.
sentences.zh: 每个新医生都要求做新的血液检查，一些是查维生素缺乏症，另一些是查类风湿性关节炎等自身免疫性疾病。

sentences.en: But when none of those tests could point to an obvious cause, I fell into the mystery bucket.
sentences.zh: 但当这些检查都无法指出明显原因时，我便落入了神秘的桶里。

sentences.en: Not the fascinating, fun kind of mystery that gets solved by a medical savant.
sentences.zh: 不是那种由医学奇才解决的迷人、有趣的神秘事件。

sentences.en: This was the other kind, in which you are punted from doctor to doctor until you run out of
sentences.zh: 这是另一种，你被像踢皮球一样从一个医生踢到另一个医生，直到你找不到

sentences.en: specialists, who, this being real life, are far too overscheduled to fixate on one patient's oddball symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 专家为止，而现实生活中，他们日程排得太满，根本无暇关注某个病人的古怪症状。

sentences.en: Even if they had, it's not clear that they could have done much.
sentences.zh: 即使他们关注了，也不清楚他们能做多少事情。

sentences.en: The options for treating pain are limited, and almost all have drawbacks.
sentences.zh: 治疗疼痛的选择很有限，而且几乎都有副作用。

sentences.en: Yes, many medications cause fatigue or nausea.
sentences.zh: 是的，许多药物会引起疲劳或恶心。

sentences.en: A weird number cause constipation.
sentences.zh: 数量惊人的药物会导致便秘。

sentences.en: When I started taking gabapentin, an anti-seizure drug that reduces the signal from the brain
sentences.zh: 当我开始服用加巴喷丁时，这是一种减少从大脑

sentences.en: to the peripheral nerves, I became forgetful and started confusing words, saying phoenix for pheasant or blue for green.
sentences.zh: 到周围神经信号的抗癫痫药，我变得健忘，开始混淆词语，把雉鸡说成凤凰，或者把绿色说成蓝色。

sentences.en: That would have been fine if the medication actually worked.
sentences.zh: 如果药物真的起效了，那倒也还好。

sentences.en: Instead, it just made things slightly less awful.
sentences.zh: 相反，它只是让情况稍微没那么糟糕而已。

sentences.en: So, like many people with chronic pain, I started trying things on my own.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像许多慢性疼痛患者一样，我开始自己尝试各种方法。

sentences.en: I went to a physical therapist, a chiropractor, and two different acupuncturists.
sentences.zh: 我去看了一位物理治疗师、一位脊椎按摩师和两位不同的针灸师。

sentences.en: I tried Feldenkrais and something called nerve flossing, a set of funky gliding arm movements, which helped a bit.
sentences.zh: 我尝试了费登奎斯疗法和一种叫做神经滑动的疗法，这是一组时髦的手臂滑动动作，起了一点作用。

sentences.en: When an appointment finally opened up at my local medical center's pain clinic, six months later, the doctor there told me that this kind of unexplained nerve pain just happens
sentences.zh: 六个月后，当我当地医疗中心的疼痛诊所终于有预约名额时，那里的医生告诉我，这种原因不明的神经痛有时就是会发生，

sentences.en: sometimes, and that it might get better in months, or years, or never.
sentences.zh: 而且可能会在几个月、几年后好转，或者永远不会好转。

sentences.en: That was just how it went.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: And no one knew why.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人知道为什么。

sentences.en: For a long time, I assumed that what happened to me was just bad luck.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，我以为发生在我身上的事只是运气不好。

sentences.en: Everyone else seemed so hardy, going for jogs, typing away for hours in cafes.
sentences.zh: 其他人看起来都那么健壮，去慢跑，在咖啡馆里打字几个小时。

sentences.en: But what I discovered over the next year was that chronic pain is everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但在接下来的一年里，我发现慢性疼痛无处不在。

sentences.en: There was the colleague who developed an autoimmune-like disease after being bitten by a virus-carrying mosquito.
sentences.zh: 有同事在被携带病毒的蚊子叮咬后患上了类似自身免疫性疾病的病。

sentences.en: A friend, John, who had a bad reaction to an antibiotic and ended up with disabling full-body nerve pain that lasted for years.
sentences.zh: 朋友约翰对抗生素产生了不良反应，最终导致了持续多年的致残性全身神经痛。

sentences.en: A former student who dislocated her shoulder in a crash and now has chronic neck pain and tension headaches.
sentences.zh: 一个前学生在车祸中肩膀脱臼，现在患有慢性颈痛和紧张性头痛。

sentences.en: Another friend's cousin who developed terrible pain after abdominal surgery, pain that left
sentences.zh: 另一个朋友的表弟在腹部手术后出现了可怕的疼痛，这种疼痛让他

sentences.en: him incapacitated for months until, bizarrely, another, unrelated surgery caused it to disappear.
sentences.zh: 数月丧失行动能力，直到诡异的是，另一次毫不相干的手术让它消失了。

sentences.en: I didn't know any of this before my own mystery ailment began because chronic pain, like chronic illness, is mostly invisible.
sentences.zh: 在我自己的神秘疾病开始之前，我对此一无所知，因为慢性疼痛和慢性疾病一样，大多是看不见的。

sentences.en: My friend John told almost no one during the years he was disabled, in part because he didn't want to be defined by his condition.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友约翰在他残疾的几年里几乎没有对任何人说起过，部分原因是他不想被自己的病情所定义。

sentences.en: My colleague admitted that many of her co-workers would be surprised to learn that she had been working in pain for years.
sentences.zh: 我的同事承认，她的许多同事如果得知她带着疼痛工作多年，会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Altogether, according to a 2011 Institute of Medicine report, roughly 100 million Americans, almost one-third of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，根据2011年医学研究所的一份报告，大约1万名美国人，几乎占美国人口的

sentences.en: population, have chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 人口的三分之一，患有慢性疼痛。

sentences.en: More than have diabetes, heart disease, and cancer combined.
sentences.zh: 比患有糖尿病、心脏病和癌症的人数总和还要多。

sentences.en: Globally, some studies put the number at 2 billion.
sentences.zh: 在全球范围内，一些研究将这个数字定为20亿。

sentences.en: Despite this, the study of pain has long been neglected.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，对疼痛的研究长期以来一直被忽视。

sentences.en: The National Institutes of Health has no center devoted to pain, and for decades, pain research
sentences.zh: 美国国立卫生研究院没有专门研究疼痛的中心，几十年来，疼痛研究所获得的经费

sentences.en: received only a fraction of the funding that went to the study of illnesses like heart disease and diabetes.
sentences.zh: 只占心脏病和糖尿病等疾病研究经费的一小部分。

sentences.en: One reason for this, paradoxically, is that pain is a part of so many different conditions.
sentences.zh: 矛盾的是，原因之一是疼痛是如此众多不同疾病的一部分。

sentences.en: It touches on cancer.
sentences.zh: 它涉及癌症。

sentences.en: It touches on neurodegeneration.
sentences.zh: 它涉及神经退行性变。

sentences.en: It touches on diabetes.
sentences.zh: 它涉及糖尿病。

sentences.en: It touches on biomechanics and injury.
sentences.zh: 它涉及生物力学和损伤。

sentences.en: It touches on mental health, says Robert Giroux, who directs the Washington University Pain Center in St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 它涉及心理健康，圣路易斯华盛顿大学疼痛中心主任罗伯特·吉鲁说。

sentences.en: Because it's everywhere, it's sort of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 因为它无处不在，所以它有点无处可寻。

sentences.en: As a result, our understanding of pain, and especially chronic pain, is far behind where it should be.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们对疼痛，尤其是慢性疼痛的理解，远远落后于应有的水平。

sentences.en: We don't know what causes a person with an injury to develop chronic pain, or why it happens in some people and not others, or why it happens more often in women.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道是什么导致受伤的人患上慢性疼痛，也不知道为什么它发生在某些人身上而不是其他人身上，或者为什么它更常发生在女性身上。

sentences.en: At a genetic and cellular level, we don't know which systems get out of whack, or why, or how to fix them.
sentences.zh: 在基因和细胞水平上，我们不知道哪些系统出了问题，为什么出问题，或者如何修复它们。

sentences.en: It took the opioid epidemic to make government agencies finally recognize the scale of the
sentences.zh: 阿片类药物流行才使政府机构终于认识到问题的严重性，

sentences.en: problem, and the fact that millions of people with chronic pain had frighteningly few options.
sentences.zh: 以及数百万慢性疼痛患者惊人地缺乏选择的事实。

sentences.en: Until recently, it had been two decades since a new drug, one that wasn't an opioid, was approved for treating pain.
sentences.zh: 直到最近，距离有一种非阿片类的新止痛药获批已经过去二十年了。

sentences.en: The aftermath of the epidemic caused other probleMs.
sentences.zh: 药物流行带来的后果引发了其他问题。

sentences.en: Doctors increasingly suspected pain patients of feigning symptoms to get drugs, leaving some
sentences.zh: 医生越来越怀疑疼痛患者是装病来获取药物，导致一些

sentences.en: people with chronic conditions scrambling for effective treatments, and the lack of alternatives escalated a long-standing sense of frustration and despair.
sentences.zh: 患有慢性病的患者为了寻求有效的治疗而四处奔波，而缺乏替代方案则加剧了长期存在的沮丧和绝望感。

sentences.en: The truth is that we've failed people in pain, one clinician admitted.
sentences.zh: 事实是我们辜负了痛苦中的人，一位临床医生承认。

sentences.en: If we had invested in understanding this years ago, we might have been able to prevent a lot of suffering.
sentences.zh: 如果我们多年前就投入资金去理解这一点，我们本可以预防很多痛苦。

sentences.en: Now, that may finally be changing.
sentences.zh: 现在，这种情况可能终于要改变了。

sentences.en: In 2018, the National Institutes of Health started the $3.9 billion HEAL initiative, a major effort
sentences.zh: 2018年，美国国立卫生研究院启动了耗资39亿美元的HEAL计划，这是一项重大努力，

sentences.en: focused on addressing the opioid crisis and figuring out the underlying mechanisms of pain in order to develop more precise, sophisticated, and personalized treatments.
sentences.zh: 旨在解决阿片类药物危机并弄清疼痛的潜在机制，以便开发更精准、更先进、更个性化的治疗方法。

sentences.en: Alan Basbaum, who oversees a pain research lab at the University of California, San Francisco, made an analogy to recent breakthroughs in cancer research.
sentences.zh: 阿兰·巴斯鲍姆（Alan Basbaum）在旧金山加利福尼亚大学监督一个疼痛研究实验室，他将近期癌症研究的突破做了一个类比。

sentences.en: For decades, cancer treatment focused on where a tumor was located—liver, stomach, lung.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，癌症治疗一直侧重于肿瘤所在的部位——肝脏、胃、肺。

sentences.en: But when researchers were finally able to study those tumors at a genetic and cellular level, that insight led to far more targeted and individualized treatments, including the
sentences.zh: 但当研究人员终于能够在基因和细胞水平上研究这些肿瘤时，这一洞察带来了更具针对性和个体化的治疗方法，包括

sentences.en: immunotherapies that recently won a Nobel Prize.
sentences.zh: 最近荣获诺贝尔奖的免疫疗法。

sentences.en: Pain research today is where cancer research was 20 years ago, Basbaum told me.
sentences.zh: 巴斯鲍姆告诉我，今天的疼痛研究就像20年前的癌症研究一样。

sentences.en: The good news is that we're able to move so much faster now.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，我们现在能够以快得多的速度前进。

sentences.en: Scientists are already closing in on one biological mechanism with the potential to significantly lessen pain, and a number of other approaches are being explored.
sentences.zh: 科学家们已经在锁定一种具有显著减轻疼痛潜力的生物机制，同时也在探索许多其他方法。

sentences.en: But the real revolution may be a new understanding of pain's complexity, an illumination of its hidden workings.
sentences.zh: 但真正的革命可能在于对疼痛复杂性的全新理解，以及对其隐藏运作机制的阐明。

sentences.en: One big reason chronic pain has been undertreated and shrugged off for decades is that medicine tends to trivialize conditions it lacks the tools to explain.
sentences.zh: 慢性病被长期低估和忽视的一个重大原因，是医学往往会轻视那些缺乏合理解释工具的病症。

sentences.en: The chronic pain revolution we need is one that won't end until we really understand why millions of people are suffering and how to offer them meaningful relief.
sentences.zh: 我们所需要的慢性疼痛革命，直到真正理解为什么数百万人正在受苦以及如何为他们提供实质性缓解之前，是不会结束的。

sentences.en: Chronic pain has traditionally been seen as a symptom.
sentences.zh: 传统上，慢性疼痛一直被视为一种症状。

sentences.en: We die in pain, we don't die of pain.
sentences.zh: 我们在痛苦中死去，但并非死于痛苦。

sentences.en: Now researchers are recognizing that chronic pain can be a disease in its own right, a disorder
sentences.zh: 现在研究人员认识到，慢性疼痛本身就可以是一种疾病，是一种

sentences.en: that happens when the nerves in our body, either peripheral ones like those in our limbs, or central ones like those running from our spinal cord to our brain, become hyperactive
sentences.zh: 当我们的身体神经——无论是四肢等外周神经，还是从脊髓延伸到大脑等中枢神经——变得过度活跃

sentences.en: or sensitized.
sentences.zh: 或致敏时所发生的紊乱。

sentences.en: This can happen for a host of reasons.
sentences.zh: 这种情况可能由多种原因引起。

sentences.en: Roughly 1 in 7 people who have surgery to fix a hernia will develop chronic pain, and millions of people have hernia surgery every year.
sentences.zh: 大约七分之一接受疝气修复手术的人会发展出慢性疼痛，而每年有数百万人接受疝气手术。

sentences.en: The risk for breast surgeries, including mastectomy, is even higher, between 40 and 60 percent.
sentences.zh: 乳腺手术（包括乳房切除术）的风险甚至更高，在40%到60%之间。

sentences.en: And the pain is frequently severe, an average of 8 on a 10-point scale, or roughly the same as patients who have had a limb amputated.
sentences.zh: 而且疼痛往往很剧烈，在10分制中平均为8分，大致相当于截肢患者感受到的疼痛。

sentences.en: Some of those people recover, or manage to get by, but others become so incapacitated that they can't work, and sometimes can barely function.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人恢复了，或者勉强应付过去了，但另一些人却丧失了劳动能力，以至于无法工作，有时甚至几乎无法维持正常生活。

sentences.en: People over a certain age, or who have diabetes or cancer, will often develop neuropathies, damaged nerves that cause constant burning and numbness.
sentences.zh: 超过一定年龄的人，或者患有糖尿病或癌症的人，经常会患上神经病变，即导致持续灼痛和麻木的受损神经。

sentences.en: And then there are the car accidents, sports injuries, and other kinds of damage, injuries that people generally recover from, except when they don't.
sentences.zh: 还有车祸、运动损伤和其他类型的损伤，人们通常能从这些损伤中恢复过来，除非他们恢复不了。

sentences.en: Mikel Curatalo, a clinician and researcher at the University of Washington Pain Management
sentences.zh: 华盛顿大学疼痛管理中心的临床医生兼研究人员米克尔·库拉塔洛（Mikel Curatalo）

sentences.en: Center, describes seeing people whose lives have been utterly and unexpectedly derailed.
sentences.zh: 描述了那些生活被彻底且出乎意料地毁掉的人。

sentences.en: I have patients, even very young patients, with headache, who can't bear any kind of light,
sentences.zh: 库拉塔洛说，我有一些病人，甚至是极年轻的病人，他们患有头痛，无法忍受任何光线，

sentences.en: Curatalo says.
sentences.zh: 库拉塔洛说。

sentences.en: They're always in the dark.
sentences.zh: 他们总是待在黑暗中。

sentences.en: They have a migraine 24-7.
sentences.zh: 他们24小时7天都在偏头痛。

sentences.en: Another patient, in her 30s, was in such pain that she couldn't get out of bed without help, but no one could figure out why.
sentences.zh: 另一位30多岁的病人痛得没有帮助就无法下床，但没有人能找出原因。

sentences.en: For these patients, Curatalo says, if they come to me, they can get maybe 20% or 30% relief, which is important, but they also don't have their life back in any way.
sentences.zh: 库拉塔洛说，对于这些患者来说，如果他们来找我，或许能缓解20%或30%，这很重要，但他们的生活并没有真正恢复正常。

sentences.en: The causes of these problems have long been mysterious.
sentences.zh: 这些问题的成因长期以来一直是个谜。

sentences.en: For years, researchers were baffled by the fact that some people with relatively mild tissue
sentences.zh: 多年来，研究人员感到困惑的是，为什么有些组织损伤相对较轻的人会经历可怕的疼痛，而其他人尽管损伤严重却感觉大多良好。

sentences.en: damage would experience terrible pain, while others with severe damage would feel mostly fine.
sentences.zh: 受到损伤的人会经历剧烈的疼痛，而另一些严重受损的人却感觉大多良好。

sentences.en: This was true regardless of whether the injury was an endometrial lesion, whiplash, or osteoarthritis.
sentences.zh: 无论是子宫内膜病变、挥鞭样损伤还是骨关节炎，情况都是如此。

sentences.en: No one understood how this could be true, Bassbaum says.
sentences.zh: 巴斯鲍姆说，没有人理解为什么会这样。

sentences.en: It just didn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 这根本说不通。

sentences.en: Ordinarily, when a person is injured, the body releases a flood of chemicals that spur healing processes, like inflammation.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，当一个人受伤时，身体会释放大量化学物质来刺激炎症等愈合过程。

sentences.en: Those same chemicals also activate our nociceptors, or pain fibers, a set of peripheral nerve endings
sentences.zh: 这些相同的化学物质也会激活我们的伤害感受器或疼痛纤维，这是一组外周神经末梢，

sentences.en: that alert the brain to tissue damage and that exist in our skin, muscles, stomach, and even internal organs.
sentences.zh: 它们向大脑发出组织受损的警报，存在于我们的皮肤、肌肉、胃甚至内脏器官中。

sentences.en: Typically, that process lasts just while an injury is healing.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，这个过程只持续到伤口愈合为止。

sentences.en: But in some cases, those pain signals keep firing, driven by what researchers now think is a complex set of genetic, endocrinological, and immunologic processes.
sentences.zh: 但在某些情况下，这些疼痛信号会持续发射，由研究人员现在认为是一组复杂的基因、内分泌和免疫过程所驱动。

sentences.en: The discovery that the pain signaling chain itself could become faulty was a crucial shift.
sentences.zh: 发现疼痛信号传导链本身会出现故障是一个关键的转变。

sentences.en: Nociceptors are essentially bundles of sensors attached to long, thin nerves that run all the way up to the brain, which in turn send signals back down to the site of injury.
sentences.zh: 伤害感受器本质上是连接到长而细的神经上的传感器束，这些神经一直延伸到大脑，而大脑反过来又向受伤部位发送信号。

sentences.en: Along the way, pain signals pass through gates, neurological filters located in the spinal cord that release chemicals to either amplify a pain signal or turn it down.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，疼痛信号会穿过关卡，即位于脊髓中的神经过滤器，它们会释放化学物质来放大疼痛信号或将其调低。

sentences.en: It's now thought that chronic pain can be caused by problems at any point along the chain.
sentences.zh: 现在人们认为，慢性疼痛可能是由该链条上任何一点的问题引起的。

sentences.en: In some cases, the problem might be the nociceptor itself, triggered by inflammation, as happens with autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis and lupus.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，问题可能是伤害感受器本身，由炎症引发，就像类风湿性关节炎和狼疮等自身免疫性疾病中发生的那样。

sentences.en: In others, the problem might be hyperactivity in the spinal cord, the brain, or both.
sentences.zh: 在另一些情况下，问题可能是脊髓、大脑或两者的过度活跃。

sentences.en: In still other cases, the cause is unclear.
sentences.zh: 在还有的其他情况下，原因尚不清楚。

sentences.en: Fibromyalgia and irritable bowel syndrome, which is considered a chronic pain condition,
sentences.zh: 纤维肌痛和肠易激综合征（被视为一种慢性疼痛病症）

sentences.en: are both driven by overactive signaling, either by the central nervous system or by the nociceptors in our muscles or gut.
sentences.zh: 都是由中枢神经系统或肌肉或肠道中的伤害感受器发出的过度活跃信号驱动的。

sentences.en: But it's not clear how or why the switch for that hyperactivity gets flipped.
sentences.zh: 但目前尚不清楚这种过度活跃的开关是如何或为什么被打开的。

sentences.en: One of the big insights of the past decade is that chronic pain is a disorder of the central nervous system, Giroux told me.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁（Giroux）告诉我，过去十年里的一大深刻见解是，慢性疼痛是一种中枢神经系统的紊乱。

sentences.en: It has been a huge change in how we understand these conditions.
sentences.zh: 这是我们理解这些病症方式的巨大变化。

sentences.en: Before, we were basically just mystified by persistent pain.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，我们基本上对持续性疼痛感到十分迷茫。

sentences.en: Heart of why it took so long to grasp this is that there's no easy way to see someone's pain or to measure it, other than asking a person to rate their pain on a scale from
sentences.zh: 之所以花了这么长时间才掌握这一点，核心原因在于，除了要求人们在1到10的量表上对疼痛进行评级之外，没有简单的方法可以看到或测量某人的疼痛。

sentences.en: While it's possible to put electrodes into the spinal cords of mice to record nerve activity, or probes into the brains of macaque monkeys to observe how neurons fire in response
sentences.zh: 虽然可以将电极放入小鼠的脊髓中记录神经活动，或者将探针放入猕猴的大脑中观察神经元如何响应疼痛而放电，但在人类身上这样做并没有道德可行的方法。

sentences.en: to pain, there's no ethical way to do the same thing in people.
sentences.zh: 对于疼痛，在人类身上以同样的方式进行研究是没有道德伦理途径的。

sentences.en: And while MRI and fMRI scans can show changes in the brains of people with chronic pain, those scans are too expensive and cumbersome to work as symptom trackers.
sentences.zh: 虽然MRI和功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）扫描可以显示慢性疼痛患者大脑的变化，但这些扫描过于昂贵且笨重，无法用作症状追踪器。

sentences.en: With other diseases, you can measure the size of a tumor or see how much a person's cortex has shrunk from Alzheimer's, Giroux told me.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁告诉我，对于其他疾病，你可以测量肿瘤的大小，或者看看阿尔茨海默病导致一个人的大脑皮层萎缩了多少。

sentences.en: There's not something measurable like that for pain.
sentences.zh: 对于疼痛，并没有这样可量化的东西。

sentences.en: From a research perspective, that's been a real hurdle.
sentences.zh: 从研究的角度来看，这确实是一个巨大的障碍。

sentences.en: To overcome that, one main project funded by HEAL is focused on studying the nervous systems
sentences.zh: 为了克服这一障碍，HEAL资助的一个主要项目专注于更直接地研究慢性疼痛患者的神经系统，

sentences.en: of people with chronic pain more directly, in part by recovering malfunctioning dorsal root ganglia and trigeminal nerves from patients undergoing surgery for chronic pain, as well
sentences.zh: 部分通过从因慢性疼痛接受手术的患者以及尸体捐赠者身上回收功能失常的背根神经节和三叉神经，

sentences.en: as from cadaveric donors.
sentences.zh: 以及来自尸体捐献者的组织。

sentences.en: Those samples are then cultured and examined using a bevy of new technologies, things like
sentences.zh: 然后使用一系列新技术（例如蛋白质组学、空间转录组学和代谢组学）对这些样本进行培养和检查，以了解它们与正常组织的区别。

sentences.en: proteomics, spatial transcriptomics, and metabolomics, to see how they differ from normal tissue.
sentences.zh: 蛋白质组学、空间转录组学和代谢组学，以了解它们与正常组织的差异。

sentences.en: The goal, Giroux explained, is to identify what changes happen at a cellular level when pain becomes chronic, and to create an atlas of those mechanisms and variations.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁解释说，其目标是确定当疼痛变成慢性时细胞水平上发生了什么变化，并绘制出这些机制和变异的图谱。

sentences.en: Understanding that, he added, would ultimately open the door to precision medicine, in which
sentences.zh: 他补充说，理解这一点最终将打开精准医学的大门，

sentences.en: drugs could be designed to target those changes specifically, rather than simply blunting the pain with anti-inflammatories or opioids.
sentences.zh: 届时可以设计药物专门针对这些变化，而不是简单地用抗炎药或阿片类药物来减轻疼痛。

sentences.en: In the beginning, everyone thought they were going to find this one breakthrough pain drug that would replace opioids, Giroux said.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁说，一开始，每个人都以为会找到这种能取代阿片类药物的突破性止痛药。

sentences.en: Increasingly, though, it's looking like chronic pain, like cancer, could end up having a range
sentences.zh: 然而，越来越多的人发现，慢性疼痛就像癌症一样，最终可能会有一系列由疾病状况以及经历它的个人的特定构成所决定的基因和细胞驱动因素。

sentences.en: of genetic and cellular drivers that vary both by condition and by the particular makeup of the person experiencing it.
sentences.zh: 因疾病状况以及患者自身身体构成的不同而有所差异的遗传和细胞驱动因素。

sentences.en: What we're learning is that pain is not just one thing, Giroux added.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁补充说，我们正在了解到，疼痛不只是一单一事物。

sentences.en: It's a thousand different things, all called pain.
sentences.zh: 它是成千上万种不同的东西，都被称为疼痛。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜洛（Winnalou）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的益智游戏“Connections”，而且我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基（Sam Azersky），我每天创作游戏《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉（promesthesia）的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到的人那样。

sentences.en: For patients, too, the landscape of chronic pain is wildly varied.
sentences.zh: 对于患者来说，慢性疼痛的状况也千差万别。

sentences.en: Some people endure a miserable year of low back pain, only to have it vanish for no clear reason.
sentences.zh: 有些人忍受了一年痛苦的下腰痛，结果却无缘无故地消失了。

sentences.en: Others aren't so lucky.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则没有那么幸运。

sentences.en: A friend of a friend spent five years with extreme pain in his arms and face after roughhousing with his son.
sentences.zh: 一个朋友的朋友在与儿子打闹后，手臂和面部经历了五年的极度疼痛。

sentences.en: He had to stop working, couldn't drive, couldn't even ride in a car without a neck brace.
sentences.zh: 他不得不停止工作，无法开车，甚至不戴颈托就无法坐车。

sentences.en: His doctors prescribed endless medications, the maximum dose of gabapentin, plus duloxetine, and others.
sentences.zh: 他的医生开了无数的药物，最大剂量的加巴喷丁，加上度洛西汀等。

sentences.en: At one point, he admitted himself to a psychiatric ward because his pain was so bad that he'd become suicidal.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他住进了精神病房，因为他的痛实在太严重，导致他有了自杀倾向。

sentences.en: There, he met other people who also became suicidal after years of living with terrible pain, day in and day out.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他遇到了其他人，他们在经历长年累月的可怕疼痛后也产生了自杀倾向。

sentences.en: The thing that makes chronic pain so awful is that it's chronic, a grinding distress that never ends.
sentences.zh: 让慢性疼痛如此糟糕的原因在于它是慢性的，是一种永无止境的折磨。

sentences.en: For those with extreme pain, that's easy to understand, but even less severe cases can be miserable.
sentences.zh: 对于那些经历极度疼痛的人来说，这一点很容易理解，但即使是不那么严重的病例也会令人痛苦不堪。

sentences.en: A pain rating of 3 or 4 out of 10 sounds mild, but having it almost all the time is grueling and limiting.
sentences.zh: 10分里评3或4分听起来很轻微，但几乎一直忍受着它会让人筋疲力尽且受到极大限制。

sentences.en: Unlike a broken arm, which gets better, or tendinitis, which hurts mostly in response to overuse, chronic pain makes your whole world shrink.
sentences.zh: 与会好转的骨折或主要因过度使用而疼痛的肌腱炎不同，慢性疼痛会让你的整个世界缩小。

sentences.en: It's harder to work and to exercise and even to do the many smaller things that make life rewarding and rich.
sentences.zh: 工作、锻炼，甚至做许多让生活充满价值和丰富的小事都变得更加困难。

sentences.en: It's also lonely.
sentences.zh: 这也令人感到孤独。

sentences.en: When my arms first went crazy, I could barely function.
sentences.zh: 当我的手臂刚开始出现问题时，我几乎无法正常生活。

sentences.en: But even after the worst had passed, I saw friends rarely.
sentences.zh: 但即使在最糟糕的时期过去之后，我也很少见到朋友。

sentences.en: I still couldn't drive more than a few minutes or sit comfortably in a chair, and I felt guilty inviting people over when there wasn't anything to do.
sentences.zh: 我仍然不能开车超过几分钟，也不能舒服地坐在椅子上，当没有什么事情可做时，我为邀请别人过来感到内疚。

sentences.en: As Kristen Veasley, director and co-founder of the Chronic Pain Research Alliance, puts it, with acute pain, medications, if you take them, they get you over a hump and you go on
sentences.zh: 正如慢性疼痛研究联盟（Chronic Pain Research Alliance）主任兼联合创始人克里斯滕·维斯利（Kristen Veasley）所说，对于急性疼痛，如果你吃药，药物能帮你度过难关，然后你就可以继续

sentences.en: your way.
sentences.zh: 过你的日子。

sentences.en: What people don't realize is that when you have chronic pain, even if you're also taking meds, you rarely feel like you were before.
sentences.zh: 人们没有意识到的是，当你患有慢性疼痛时，即使你也在吃药，你也极难找回以前的感觉。

sentences.en: At best, they can reduce your pain, but usually don't eliminate it.
sentences.zh: 充其量，它们可以减轻你的疼痛，但通常无法消除它。

sentences.en: A cruel catch-22 around chronic pain is that it often leads to anxiety and depression, both of which can make pain worse.
sentences.zh: 围绕慢性疼痛的一个残酷的恶性循环是，它往往会导致焦虑和抑郁，而这两者都会使疼痛加剧。

sentences.en: That's partly because focusing on a thing can reinforce it, but also because emotional states have physical effects.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是专注于某件事会强化它，但也因为情绪状态会产生生理影响。

sentences.en: Both anxiety and depression are known to increase inflammation, which can also worsen pain.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，焦虑和抑郁都会增加炎症，这也会恶化疼痛。

sentences.en: As a result, pain management often includes cognitive behavioral therapy, meditation practice, or other coping skills.
sentences.zh: 因此，疼痛管理通常包括认知行为疗法、冥想练习或其他应对技巧。

sentences.en: But while those tools are vital, it's notoriously hard to reprogram our reactions.
sentences.zh: 但尽管这些工具至关重要，但众所周知，要重新调整我们的反应是非常困难的。

sentences.en: Our minds and bodies have evolved both to anticipate pain and to remember it, making it hard not to worry.
sentences.zh: 我们的思维和身体在进化过程中既学会了预测疼痛，也学会了记住疼痛，这使得我们很难不去担忧。

sentences.en: And because chronic pain is so uncomfortable and isolating, it's also depressing.
sentences.zh: 而且由于慢性疼痛是如此令人不适和孤立，它也让人感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Bayla Travis, a pain psychologist based in the Bay Area, notes that because chronic pain has an emotional component, people may feel ashamed if they're not able to control their
sentences.zh: 湾区的疼痛心理学家贝拉·特拉维斯（Bayla Travis）指出，由于慢性疼痛具有情感成分，如果无法控制自己的

sentences.en: symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 症状，人们可能会感到羞耻。

sentences.en: With the self-help culture we have, there's this feeling like you should be able to fix it,
sentences.zh: 在我们的自助文化中，有一种感觉，觉得你应该能够解决它，

sentences.en: Travis says.
sentences.zh: 特拉维斯说。

sentences.en: But the truth is that while things like cognitive behavioral therapy can help, you often won't be able to eliminate the pain.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，虽然认知行为疗法之类的方法可以提供帮助，但你往往无法完全消除疼痛。

sentences.en: It's still not clear why one person goes on to develop chronic pain when another doesn't.
sentences.zh: 目前仍不清楚为什么一个人会发展出慢性疼痛而另一个人不会。

sentences.en: But research has increasingly shown that some people are more susceptible.
sentences.zh: 但研究日益表明，有些人更易感。

sentences.en: Women are more likely to develop chronic pain conditions, possibly because, as Veasley noted,
sentences.zh: 女性更容易患上慢性疼痛，可能是因为，正如维斯利所指出的，

sentences.en: they're at higher risk for autoimmune disorders, and because hormonal fluctuations can aggravate chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 她们患自身免疫性疾病的风险更高，而且荷尔蒙波动会加剧慢性疼痛。

sentences.en: And once a person has one kind of chronic pain, they're more likely to develop another.
sentences.zh: 而且，一旦一个人患有一种慢性疼痛，他们就更有可能患上另一种。

sentences.en: The idea, Veasley says, is that if your central nervous system isn't functioning properly, you're more likely to develop chronic pain of some kind—migraine, temporal mandibular
sentences.zh: 维斯利说，这个想法是，如果你的中枢神经系统功能不正常，你就更有可能患上某种慢性疼痛——偏头痛、颞下颌

sentences.en: disorders, back pain, pelvic pain.
sentences.zh: 关节紊乱、背痛、盆腔痛。

sentences.en: And then, because your body isn't processing pain the way it should, you're more likely to develop other conditions.
sentences.zh: 然后，由于你的身体没有像应有的那样处理疼痛，你更有可能发展出其他病症。

sentences.en: For instance, if you have chronic pain and undergo surgery for something unrelated, you're much more likely to end up with chronic pain in that other part of your body afterward.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你患有慢性疼痛并因无关原因接受手术，你事后在身体其他部位最终患上慢性疼痛的可能性要大得多。

sentences.en: Veasley herself has had chronic pain for decades.
sentences.zh: 维斯利本人患慢性疼痛已有数十年之久。

sentences.en: As a teenager, she was hit by a car while biking home from camp and nearly killed.
sentences.zh: 在青少年时期，她骑自行车从营地回家时被一辆汽车撞倒，差点丧命。

sentences.en: The impact broke all her ribs, fractured her leg, and collapsed her lung.
sentences.zh: 这次撞击撞断了她所有的肋骨，骨折了腿，并导致肺塌陷。

sentences.en: She also lost a third of her liver and had severe internal bleeding.
sentences.zh: 她还失去了三分之一的肝脏，并伴有严重的内出血。

sentences.en: For years, just managing the resulting pain was the equivalent of a part-time job.
sentences.zh: 多年来，仅仅控制由此产生的疼痛就相当于一份兼职工作。

sentences.en: I was spending upward of 20 hours a week on physical therapy, chiropractor visits, exercise,
sentences.zh: 维斯利告诉我，我每周花在物理治疗、脊椎按摩、锻炼、

sentences.en: heat, ice, all the stuff, Veasley told me, and it cost easily $25,000 a year out of pocket.
sentences.zh: 热敷、冰敷以及所有这些事情上的时间超过20个小时，每年自掏腰包轻松花费2万5千美元。

sentences.en: The medications she tried were hit or miss, a common problem, because there's currently no way for doctors to know which pain drug is going to work for whom.
sentences.zh: 她尝试过的药物时好时坏，这是一个常见的问题，因为目前医生无法得知哪种止痛药对谁有效。

sentences.en: They also had downsides.
sentences.zh: 它们也有缺点。

sentences.en: One made her mouth so dry that she was constantly drinking water.
sentences.zh: 一种药让她的嘴巴非常干，以至于她一直在喝水。

sentences.en: Others caused her to gain 20 pounds or to feel sedated and foggy.
sentences.zh: 另一些药导致她体重增加20磅，或者感到镇静和思维模糊。

sentences.en: Yet another made her entire body itch.
sentences.zh: 还有一种药让她全身发痒。

sentences.en: Like, it turned off the pain switch, but turned on the itch switch, she says.
sentences.zh: 她说，就像是，它关闭了疼痛开关，却打开了发痒开关。

sentences.en: Ultimately, Veasley tried 14 different drugs before finding one that helped.
sentences.zh: 最终，维斯利尝试了14种不同的药物，才找到一种有帮助的。

sentences.en: I don't think people really get what goes into trying a new medication, she says.
sentences.zh: 她说，我不认为人们真正理解尝试新药需要付出什么。

sentences.en: They think, what's the big deal?
sentences.zh: 他们会想，这有什么大不了的？

sentences.en: You just take it, and if it works, it works.
sentences.zh: 你吃就行了，如果管用就管用。

sentences.en: If it doesn't, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不管用就算了。

sentences.en: But what actually happens is that you have to start on this teensy-eensy dose, and then a week later, increase to the next dose, and the next one, and then you start to get the
sentences.zh: 但实际发生的是，你必须从这种极微小的剂量开始，然后一周后，增加到下一个剂量，再下一个，接着你开始出现

sentences.en: side effects.
sentences.zh: 副作用。

sentences.en: When it doesn't work, which is most of the time, either because the drug doesn't help or the side effects are too bad, you have to do the whole thing in reverse.
sentences.zh: 当它不管用时（大多数情况都是如此，要么是因为药物没有帮助，要么是因为副作用太严重），你必须把整个过程反过来做一遍。

sentences.en: So it takes forever.
sentences.zh: 所以这需要花费极长的时间。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, you're in pain and trying to take care of your children and do your job and all the reSt.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你正承受着疼痛，还要照顾孩子、做工作以及所有其他

sentences.en: One day last fall, I met Giroux at his lab in the anesthesiology department on the Washington
sentences.zh: 去年秋天的一天，我在圣路易斯华盛顿大学校园的麻醉学系实验室里遇到了吉鲁，他在那里指导四个致力于回收和研究慢性疼痛患者组织样本的中心之一。

sentences.en: University campus in St. Louis, where he directs one of four centers devoted to recovering and studying tissue samples taken from patients with chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 位于圣路易斯的大学校园，他在那里领导着四个致力于收集和研究慢性疼痛患者组织样本的中心之一。

sentences.en: Giroux is cheerful and funny, with a gray-blonde beard and the slightly distracted air of someone who would rather be getting back to work.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁性格开朗幽默，留着灰金色的胡须，带有那种宁愿回去工作的人的略微心不在焉的神态。

sentences.en: Once on a video call, he mentioned a colleague's research study, then stared silently into space, and, sorry, he said, abashed.
sentences.zh: 有一次在视频通话中，他提到了同事的一项研究，然后默默地出神，接着略带羞涩地说，抱歉。

sentences.en: I was thinking about the study.
sentences.zh: 我在思考那项研究。

sentences.en: The lab that day was packed with graduate students and postdocs working at different stations.
sentences.zh: 那天实验室里挤满了在不同工位工作的研究生和博士后。

sentences.en: Giroux led me to a back table where Brian Kopitz, a scientist who oversees tissue procurement, retrieved a small Ziploc bag from a tray of ice pellets.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁把我带到一张后面的桌子上，负责组织采购的科学家布赖恩·科皮茨从一盘冰粒中拿出一个小自封袋。

sentences.en: Inside was a tiny beige triangle, roughly like what you'd get if you sliced off the very tip of your pinky.
sentences.zh: 里面是一个微小的米色三角形，大致就像你切下小指最尖端时得到的那样。

sentences.en: Kopitz explained that it was a dorsal root ganglion, a cluster of cells that acts as a kind of switchboard, routing signals from the periphery to the central nervous system.
sentences.zh: 科皮茨解释说，这是一个背根神经节，一簇起到某种总机作用的细胞，将信号从周围传导至中枢神经系统。

sentences.en: This one had been recovered from a thoracic vertebra and is one of several responsible for managing nerve signals in the body's trunk.
sentences.zh: 这个是从胸椎取出的，是负责管理身体躯干神经信号的几个神经节之一。

sentences.en: After gently returning it to the bag, he opened a different one and brought out a piece of fresh-frozen
sentences.zh: 轻轻将其放回袋子后，他又打开另一个袋子，拿出一块新鲜冷冻的

sentences.en: spinal cord, a red-and-white streaked nugget that looked disconcertingly like a piece of artificial crab.
sentences.zh: 脊髓，这是一块红白相间的硬块，看起来非常像一块人造蟹肉，让人心里直犯嘀咕。

sentences.en: The ability to examine tissue recovered from patients with chronic pain is a major step forward.
sentences.zh: 检查从慢性疼痛患者身上获取的组织的能力，是一个重大的进步。

sentences.en: Until recently, researchers and pharmaceutical companies studying pain primarily used mice or other animals as human proxies and would then invest years, often more than a decade,
sentences.zh: 直到最近，研究疼痛的研究人员和制药公司主要使用小鼠或其他动物作为人类的替身，然后往往会投入数年，通常超过十年的时间，

sentences.en: trying to develop a drug based on those findings.
sentences.zh: 试图根据这些发现开发药物。

sentences.en: What we learned, unfortunately, is that some of the receptors we identified in mice weren't expressed at the same level or in the same place in people, Giroux said.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁说，不幸的是，我们了解到，我们在小鼠身上发现的一些受体在人类身上的表达水平或位置并不相同。

sentences.en: When you go from animal to human and a drug fails, that's 20 years of work gone.
sentences.zh: 当你从动物转向人类而药物失败时，那就是20年的心血付诸东流。

sentences.en: That high failure rate is why many pharmaceutical companies stopped trying to develop new pain medications more than a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 正是这种高失败率，导致许多制药公司在十多年前就停止了尝试开发新的止痛药。

sentences.en: So now the idea is to go the other way, to use these new technologies to identify drug targets based on changes in human tissue, Giroux said.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁说，所以现在的想法是反其道而行之，利用这些新技术根据人体组织的变化来确定药物靶点。

sentences.en: As a first step in that process, Juliet Marigi, a postdoc in Giroux's lab, spent two months
sentences.zh: 作为该过程的第一步，吉鲁实验室的博士后朱丽叶·马里吉花了两个月时间

sentences.en: training an algorithm to identify different types of neurons and other cells in the ganglion.
sentences.zh: 训练算法来识别神经节中的不同类型神经元和其他细胞。

sentences.en: They bring fragments of live tissue here to the tissue culture room so we can see how cells change their behavior in response to pain, Marigi told me.
sentences.zh: 马里吉告诉我说，他们把活体组织的碎片带到这里的组织培养室，这样我们就能看到细胞如何响应疼痛而改变行为。

sentences.en: Marigi took me into a small cubby with a heavy black curtain around it and pulled up an image that looked like outer space, a blue-black cosmos dotted with cyan and pink galaxies.
sentences.zh: 马里吉把我带到一个周围挂着厚厚黑帘的小隔间里，调出一张看起来像外太空的图像，一个点缀着青色和粉红色星系的蓝黑色宇宙。

sentences.en: These are the different cells, she told me, pointing at the various colors.
sentences.zh: 她指着各种颜色对我说，这些是不同的细胞。

sentences.en: Sensory neurons, immune cells, Schwann cells, those responsible for protecting and repairing nerves.
sentences.zh: 感觉神经元、免疫细胞、许旺细胞，那些负责保护和修复神经的细胞。

sentences.en: The cyan ones are nociceptors.
sentences.zh: 青色的那些是伤害感受器。

sentences.en: Between the clumps of color, there were delicate gray threads that Marigi explained were axons,
sentences.zh: 在色彩斑块之间，有一些精致的灰色线条，马里吉解释说那是轴突，

sentences.en: the long nerves that connect the neurons in the dorsal root ganglion to muscles and other tissue.
sentences.zh: 即连接背根神经节中的神经元与肌肉及其他组织的的长神经。

sentences.en: A ganglion is like a bouquet of flowers, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，神经节就像一束花。

sentences.en: The axons are the steMs.
sentences.zh: 轴突就是花茎。

sentences.en: Giroux and Marigi are currently studying a cannabinoid receptor known as CB1 in hopes of finding a way to harness its analgesic properties
sentences.zh: 吉鲁和马里吉目前正在研究一种被称为CB1的大麻素受体，希望能找到一种方法来利用其镇痛特性，

sentences.en: without activating the same receptors in the brain that make cannabis psychoactive.
sentences.zh: 同时不激活大脑中使大麻产生精神活性的相同受体。

sentences.en: They're also finding new potential drug targets based on changes they see in the cells of chronic pain patients.
sentences.zh: 他们还在根据在慢性疼痛患者细胞中观察到的变化寻找新的潜在药物靶点。

sentences.en: These sorts of interventions have become possible, in part, because of radical advances in drug design.
sentences.zh: 这类干预措施之所以成为可能，部分原因在于药物设计方面的激进突破。

sentences.en: Science is just different now, Giroux said.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁说，科学现在完全不同了。

sentences.en: Thanks to new imaging technologies and computing abilities, he explained, we can get information on the structure of receptors
sentences.zh: 他解释说，多亏了新的成像技术和计算能力，我们能够以10年前不可能实现的的时间尺度获取有关受体结构

sentences.en: and how drugs attach to them on a timescale that was impossible 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 以及药物如何附着在受体上的信息。

sentences.en: Other advances are allowing researchers to rapidly gather data on the microscopic changes driving an individual patient's condition, what might be called their pain signature.
sentences.zh: 其他进展使研究人员能够迅速收集有关驱动个体患者病情的微观变化的数据，这可以被称为他们的疼痛特征。

sentences.en: That data, which could include gene and protein expression or immune phenotyping, also opens the door to tailor-made treatments.
sentences.zh: 这些数据可能包括基因和蛋白质表达或免疫表型，这也为量身定制的治疗打开了大门。

sentences.en: It's really uncanny, Giroux added.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁补充说，这真的很不可思议。

sentences.en: Basically, it means that we're going to have a lot more detail that will allow us to move much more quickly.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这意味着我们将拥有更多细节，从而使我们能够以快得多的速度推进。

sentences.en: Roughly 20 years ago, scientists made a discovery that may well hold the key to the future of pain treatment, one that could allow them to create a kind of ozempic for pain.
sentences.zh: 大约20年前，科学家们有了一项发现，这很可能是通往未来疼痛治疗的关键，这项发现可能使他们能够创造一种用于疼痛的“司美格鲁肽”。

sentences.en: In 2006, a global search found that people with mutations in a particular gene had radically different experiences of pain.
sentences.zh: 在2006年，一项全球搜寻发现，特定基因发生突变的人对疼痛的体验有着截然不同的感受。

sentences.en: Those with higher gene expression had constant burning pain.
sentences.zh: 基因表达较高的人会感到持续的灼痛。

sentences.en: Just wearing clothes could be excruciating.
sentences.zh: 仅仅穿衣服都可能是痛苦难耐的。

sentences.en: People born with no expression had no pain at all, to the point where they would cheerfully walk around with broken bones or severe burns.
sentences.zh: 天生没有这种表达的人根本感觉不到疼痛，甚至会高高兴兴地带着骨折或严重烧伤四处走动。

sentences.en: For years, researchers and pharmaceutical companies struggled to create a drug that controlled the sodium ion channel encoded by that gene, NAV 1.7.
sentences.zh: 多年来，研究人员和制药公司一直在努力研发一种能够控制该基因编码的钠离子通道NAV 1.7的药物。

sentences.en: NAV channels are essential to many things in the body that run on electricity.
sentences.zh: NAV通道对体内许多靠电力运行的事物至关重要。

sentences.en: NAV 1.5, for example, is crucial to regulating our heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 例如，NAV 1.5对于调节我们的心跳至关重要。

sentences.en: NAV 1.7 is striking because it seems to exist primarily in our nociceptors, where it acts as a kind of starting gate for pain signals,
sentences.zh: NAV 1.7引人注目是因为它似乎主要存在于我们的伤害感受器中，在那里它充当疼痛信号的某种起始闸门，

sentences.en: adjusting the permeability of cell membranes so that salts can flow through.
sentences.zh: 调节细胞膜的通透性，以便盐分能够通过。

sentences.en: Those salts, in turn, create an electrical current in sensory neurons that makes them more excitable.
sentences.zh: 这些盐分反过来在感觉神经元中产生电流，使它们更易兴奋。

sentences.en: Maddeningly, none of those efforts to control NAV 1.7 worked.
sentences.zh: 令人抓狂的是，所有这些控制NAV 1.7的努力都没有奏效。

sentences.en: Now, that may be shifting.
sentences.zh: 现在，情况可能会发生变化。

sentences.en: Last summer, the company Vertex Pharmaceuticals announced that it had had promising results for a painkiller, Cezetrogene, which worked on a related channel, NAV 1.8.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，福泰制药公司宣布，其针对相关通道NAV 1.8的止痛药Cezetrogene取得了有希望的结果。

sentences.en: If approved, it will be one of the first non-opioid painkillers to reach patients in more than 20 years.
sentences.zh: 如果获批，这将是20多年来首批触及患者的非阿片类止痛药之一。

sentences.en: The other so-called CGRP drugs were recently approved for migraines.
sentences.zh: 其他所谓的CGRP药物最近获准用于治疗偏头痛。

sentences.en: Regardless of what happens with Cezetrogene, most people I spoke to agreed that Vertex's NAV breakthrough would likely pave the way for more treatments.
sentences.zh: 无论Cezetrogene的情况如何，我交谈过的大多数人都认为，福泰制药的NAV突破很可能会为更多的治疗铺平道路。

sentences.en: The prospect of a pill that would act as a kind of volume knob for pain is especially tantalizing because studies have shown
sentences.zh: 一种可以充当疼痛音量旋钮的药丸的前景格外诱人，因为研究表明，

sentences.en: that interrupting the pain-signaling circuit in nociceptors, say by damping down NAV 1.7 or 1.8, quenches pain even in patients whose nerves have become sensitized.
sentences.zh: 中断伤害感受器中的疼痛信号传导回路（例如通过调低NAV 1.7或1.8）甚至可以消除那些神经已经敏感化的患者的疼痛。

sentences.en: One thing we know drives long-term pain are these nociceptors, notes William Renthall, whose lab at Harvard studies migraine and chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 哈佛大学研究偏头痛和慢性疼痛的实验室的威廉·伦索尔指出，我们知道导致长期疼痛的一个因素就是这些伤害感受器。

sentences.en: So if we can target those selectively, it gives us a lot of shots on goal, meaning therapeutics that will work on many, many, if not most, people.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们能够有选择性地针对它们，这就给了我们很多次击球得分的机会，这意味着这些疗法将在许多、许多人（如果不是大多数人的话）身上起作用。

sentences.en: Drugs in general work by binding to a particular receptor, sometimes with the goal of inhibiting it, sometimes to make it speed up production of a particular molecule,
sentences.zh: 药物通常通过与特定受体结合来起作用，有时目的是抑制它，有时是使其加速生产特定分子，

sentences.en: which in turn triggers other processes.
sentences.zh: 这反过来又会触发其他过程。

sentences.en: The problem, at least until now, is that the same receptors we target to dull pain also turn up elsewhere in our body.
sentences.zh: 问题是，至少到目前为止，我们用来减轻疼痛的相同受体也会出现在我们身体的其他地方。

sentences.en: Opioid receptors, for instance, are everywhere, in our sensory nerve endings, but also in our gut and brain, which is why opioids block pain,
sentences.zh: 例如，阿片受体无处不在，在我们的感觉神经末梢中，也在我们的肠道和大脑中，这就是为什么阿片类药物能阻断疼痛，

sentences.en: but also cause constipation and euphoria, and can depress respiratory function.
sentences.zh: 但也会引起便秘和欣快感，并且会抑制呼吸功能。

sentences.en: Even over-the-counter drugs like ibuprofen,
sentences.zh: 即使是像布洛芬这样的非处方药，

sentences.en: Advil, have issues.
sentences.zh: Advil，也有问题。

sentences.en: Ibuprofen limits inflammation by inhibiting a set of enzymes known as cyclooxygenase.
sentences.zh: 布洛芬通过抑制一组被称为环氧合酶的酶来限制炎症。

sentences.en: But doing that also inhibits production of prostaglandin, a molecule that, among other things, is involved in protecting and repairing the mucosa in our gut,
sentences.zh: 但这样做也会抑制前列腺素的产生，这种分子除了别的功能外，还参与保护和修复肠道黏膜，

sentences.en: which is why ibuprofen can cause peptic ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么布洛芬会引起消化性溃疡和胃肠道出血。

sentences.en: I'm a big believer in drugs,
sentences.zh: 加州大学旧金山分校的科学家巴斯鲍姆说，

sentences.en: Bassbaum, the UCSF scientist says, but drugs don't know where to go.
sentences.zh: 我非常相信药物的作用，但药物不知道该去哪里。

sentences.en: To fix that,
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，

sentences.en: Bassbaum is trying to create targeted analgesics, drugs that bind only to the nerve receptors controlling pain and not to receptors in the brain.
sentences.zh: 巴斯鲍姆正试图创造靶向镇痛药，这些药物只与控制疼痛的神经受体结合，而不与大脑中的受体结合。

sentences.en: This is a complicated problem of medicinal chemistry,
sentences.zh: 巴斯鲍姆承认，这是一个复杂的药物化学问题，

sentences.en: Bassbaum admits, but not impossible.
sentences.zh: 但并非不可能。

sentences.en: There's even a precedent of sorts,
sentences.zh: 甚至可以说有一种先例，

sentences.en: Weirdly, the over-the-counter anti-diarrheal medication Imodium is an opioid, just one that binds to receptors in the gut, but is kept out of the brain by guardian molecules
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，非处方止泻药易蒙停是一种阿片类药物，只是它与肠道中的受体结合，但被被称为转运蛋白的守护分子挡在了大脑之外。

sentences.en: known as transporters.
sentences.zh: 转运蛋白。

sentences.en: Other efforts are also promising.
sentences.zh: 其他努力也很有前景。

sentences.en: Giroux told me about a colleague who developed a treatment, now being pursued by Eli Lilly, that may ease peripheral neuropathy by slowing degeneration in nerves.
sentences.zh: 吉鲁告诉我，他的一位同事开发了一种疗法，目前正由礼来公司推进，该疗法可能通过减缓神经退化来缓解周围神经病变。

sentences.en: And researchers at Yale and the Veterans Administration recently found that blocking NAV 1.7 channels with carbamazepine, a drug used to treat epilepsy and trigeminal neuralgia,
sentences.zh: 耶鲁大学和退伍军人事务部的研究人员最近发现，用卡马西平（一种用于治疗癫痫和三叉神经痛的药物）阻断NAV 1.7通道，

sentences.en: could stop the joint damage and pain caused by osteoarthritis.
sentences.zh: 可以阻止由骨关节炎引起的关节损伤和疼痛。

sentences.en: There's also a growing awareness that chronic pain requires individualized treatment plans and ongoing support.
sentences.zh: 人们也越来越意识到，慢性疼痛需要个体化的治疗方案和持续的支持。

sentences.en: Some medical centers have created pain clinics specifically for patients with chronic pain, with resources including acupuncture and physical therapy,
sentences.zh: 一些医疗中心专门为慢性疼痛患者设立了疼痛诊所，提供包括针灸和物理治疗在内的资源，

sentences.en: as well as specialized pain pharmacists, psychologists, and physicians, all under one roof.
sentences.zh: 以及专门的疼痛药剂师、心理学家和医生，全部集中在同一屋檐下。

sentences.en: For people living with chronic pain, it's almost like being in a long-term relationship, notes Uda Maeda, a clinical psychologist who specializes in helping people manage pain.
sentences.zh: 专门帮助人们管理疼痛的临床心理学家宇田前指出，对于生活在慢性疼痛中的人来说，这几乎就像是在谈一场长期恋爱。

sentences.en: An analogy I use with my clients is that your pain is like this destructive, obnoxious roommate that's always interfering in your daily life, but it's a roommate you cannot evict.
sentences.zh: 我和客户使用的一个比喻是，你的疼痛就像这个总是干涉你日常生活的具有破坏性、令人讨厌的室友，但这是一个你无法赶走的室友。

sentences.en: So instead of feeling like you're battling your body every day, it's like how do I work with this body on a daily basis and have a healthy coexistence with it?
sentences.zh: 因此，与其觉得你每天都在与自己的身体作斗争，不如想想我如何每天与这个身体合作并与它和平共处？

sentences.en: One day last fall, I drove to visit one of these new clinics, the Center for Pain Medicine at the University of California, San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 去年秋天的某一天，我开车去参观其中一家新诊所，即加州大学旧金山分校疼痛医学中心。

sentences.en: The center, which was previously located in a dingy, isolated building, now occupied part of a sunny, custom-built floor with tall windows overlooking the bay.
sentences.zh: 该中心以前位于一栋昏暗、孤立的建筑里，现在占据了一个阳光充足、定制建造的楼层的一部分，高大的窗户俯瞰着海湾。

sentences.en: Chris Abrecht, the medical director, led me through, pointing out procedure areas for ultrasound-guided nerve blocks, trigger point injections, and other treatments,
sentences.zh: 医疗主任克里斯·阿尔布雷希特带我参观，指出了用于超声引导下神经阻滞、触发点注射和其他治疗的操作区，

sentences.en: therapy offices, and even an infusion area where the psychoactive anesthetic ketamine or other drugs can be administered.
sentences.zh: 治疗室，甚至还有一个输液区，在那里可以施用精神活性麻醉剂氯胺酮或其他药物。

sentences.en: Then he took me to see Julian Motzkin, a neurologiSt.
sentences.zh: 然后他带我去见神经学家朱利安·莫茨金。

sentences.en: That afternoon, Motzkin was meeting a new patient, a soft-spoken former EMT in his 40s who had experienced chronic migraine headaches since childhood
sentences.zh: 那天下午，莫茨金正在会见一位新病人，一位40多岁、说话温和的前紧急医疗救护员，他从小就经历慢性偏头痛，

sentences.en: and who had already tried an extensive list of medications and other treatments, most new since 2020, when his symptoms abruptly became worse.
sentences.zh: 并且已经尝试过大量的药物和其他治疗方法，其中大多数是2020年症状突然恶化以来出现的新药。

sentences.en: As Motzkin typed notes, the man recalled that on a recent visit to another prestigious university pain clinic, the doctor opened by saying,
sentences.zh: 当莫茨金在打笔记时，这名男子回忆起最近去另一所著名大学疼痛诊所就诊时，医生一开口就说，

sentences.en: I'm probably not going to be able to help you.
sentences.zh: 我可能帮不了你。

sentences.en: For the next 90 minutes, Motzkin asked questions and listened, as the man gave precise, medically detailed answers.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的90分钟里，莫茨金一边提问一边倾听，而该男子则给出了精确的、具有医学专业细节的回答。

sentences.en: By the end, he had identified one possible overlooked cause and two potentially promising treatments.
sentences.zh: 到最后，他确定了一个可能被忽视的病因和两个具有潜在前景的疗法。

sentences.en: But what was most striking to me was the sheer power of Motzkin's attentiveness.
sentences.zh: 但最让我震惊的是莫茨金专注力的纯粹力量。

sentences.en: Afterward, I felt relieved just to know that Motzkin existed and couldn't help wishing that I'd seen him when my own pain started.
sentences.zh: 事后，光是知道莫茨金的存在就让我感到宽慰，我不禁希望在我的疼痛刚开始时就能去看他。

sentences.en: This kind of detailed, time-consuming approach is one that many patients with severe chronic pain need, but that is vanishingly hard to find.
sentences.zh: 这种详细、耗时的方法是许多严重慢性疼痛患者所需要的，但却极其难找。

sentences.en: When I talked to Motzkin later, he told me that patients often come to him after having bad experiences with other doctors or even other pain clinics.
sentences.zh: 后来我和莫茨金交谈时，他告诉我，患者经常在与其他医生甚至其他疼痛诊所有过糟糕的经历后来找他。

sentences.en: It's kind of shocking to me, Motzkin said.
sentences.zh: 莫茨金说，这对我来说有点震惊。

sentences.en: For so many people with pain, interacting with the healthcare system often makes their suffering worse.
sentences.zh: 对于如此多的疼痛患者来说，与医疗系统的互动往往会加剧他们的痛苦。

sentences.en: It just drives me nuts.
sentences.zh: 这真让我发疯。

sentences.en: The profit-driven nature of medicine, with its insurance-coded procedures and increasingly high caseloads, is one part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 医学的利润驱动本质，伴随着其医疗保险编码的手术和日益繁重的病例量，是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: But it's also true that doctors often aren't comfortable treating patients with chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 但同样真实的是，医生往往对治疗慢性疼痛患者感到不自在。

sentences.en: One of the challenges is that, in many places, pain is still a subspecialty rotation within anesthesia,
sentences.zh: 莫茨金解释说，其中一个挑战是，在许多地方，疼痛仍然是麻醉学内的一个亚专科轮转。

sentences.en: Motzkin explained.
sentences.zh: 莫茨金解释说。

sentences.en: So for medical students to get exposure to these issues in a meaningful way, they usually have to do an elective in anesthesia and then a subelective in pain.
sentences.zh: 因此，医学生要以有意义的方式接触这些问题，通常必须选修麻醉学，然后选修疼痛科。

sentences.en: On top of that, many doctors simply don't like chronic pain patients, whom they often see as demanding and frustrating, an unsolvable problem they quickly tire of.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，许多医生根本不喜欢慢性疼痛患者，他们经常认为这些患者要求高、令人沮丧，是一个他们很快就会厌倦的无法解决的问题。

sentences.en: A surprising number of doctors and nurses, when they hear what I do, say, I can't believe you deal with these difficult patients.
sentences.zh: 当听到我的工作内容时，惊人数量的医生和护士会说，我不敢相信你能应付这些难缠的病人。

sentences.en: They're so hard.
sentences.zh: 他们太难对付了。

sentences.en: They're so terrible to work with,
sentences.zh: 和他们共事太糟糕了，

sentences.en: Motzkin said.
sentences.zh: 莫茨金说。

sentences.en: It's so much stigma.
sentences.zh: 这有着太多的污名化。

sentences.en: Just the other day, Motzkin told me he saw a man who had a long history of back and muscle pain, but who was experiencing alarming new symptoms, numbness, difficulty walking,
sentences.zh: 莫茨金告诉我，就在前几天，他看到了一名男子，该男子有长期背部和肌肉疼痛病史，但正在经历令人担忧的新症状，麻木、行走困难，

sentences.en: and several months of extreme escalating discomfort.
sentences.zh: 以及几个月来极端不断升级的不适。

sentences.en: And what he was told was, hey, you're a pain guy.
sentences.zh: 而他被告知的是，嘿，你是个疼痛患者。

sentences.en: This is just some more pain that you're having.
sentences.zh: 这只是你正在经历的一些更多的疼痛罢了。

sentences.en: I don't know what to tell you.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该对你说什么。

sentences.en: Maybe we can adjust your meds.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以调整一下你的药量。

sentences.en: After seeing the patient,
sentences.zh: 在看过这名病人后，

sentences.en: Motzkin reviewed an MRI of his neck and found a lesion on his spinal cord, a possible sign of multiple sclerosis.
sentences.zh: 莫茨金查阅了他颈部的核磁共振成像，发现脊髓上有一个病变，这可能是多发性硬化症的迹象。

sentences.en: When Motzkin told the man about the lesion and that it might be contributing to his new symptoms, the man started to cry.
sentences.zh: 当莫茨金将这个病变以及它可能导致其新症状的情况告诉这个人时，这个人哭了。

sentences.en: Not because of what the scan found, but because someone had finally listened and taken his experience seriously.
sentences.zh: 不是因为扫描发现了什么，而是因为终于有人倾听并认真对待他的经历了。

sentences.en: He'd basically given up, Motzkin said.
sentences.zh: 莫茨金说，他基本上已经放弃了。

sentences.en: He'd been treated like he was overreacting, that nothing had changed.
sentences.zh: 他被当作反应过度对待，仿佛一切都没有改变。

sentences.en: But that wasn't true.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: This attitude is deeply rooted.
sentences.zh: 这种态度根深蒂固。

sentences.en: For years, Motzkin noted, people with migraines were often institutionalized and in some cases, even lobotomized.
sentences.zh: 莫茨金指出，多年来，偏头痛患者经常被送进收容所，在某些情况下甚至接受了脑叶切除术。

sentences.en: Then, in the 1950s, a drug called methasurgide was discovered that prevented migraine in a huge number of people.
sentences.zh: 然后，在20世纪50年代，人们发现了一种名为甲麦角酰胺的药物，它能预防大量人群的偏头痛。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, he said, migraine stopped being a psychiatric diagnosis and became a medical condition.
sentences.zh: 他说，突然之间，偏头痛不再是一种精神病诊断，而变成了一种医疗状况。

sentences.en: There are many similar examples, conditions that were initially misdiagnosed or dismissed, either because doctors didn't understand them
sentences.zh: 有许多类似的例子，这些病情最初被误诊或驳回，要么是因为医生不理解它们，

sentences.en: or because they didn't yet have the right test or treatment.
sentences.zh: 要么是因为他们还没有合适的检测方法或治疗方法。

sentences.en: That continues to be true.
sentences.zh: 这种情况依然存在。

sentences.en: We still have no good way to measure dysfunction in pain and temperature nerves, and no way to reliably quantify changes in our brain's pain circuit.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然没有好的方法来测量疼痛和温度神经的功能障碍，也没有办法可靠地量化我们大脑疼痛回路的变化。

sentences.en: When it comes to pain, Motzkin said, we don't have the tools yet.
sentences.zh: 莫茨金说，说到疼痛，我们还没有相应的工具。

sentences.en: Still, he thinks things are starting to change.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他认为事情正在开始改变。

sentences.en: We're getting very close to the kind of large-scale, personalized medicine that will prevent a lot of patient suffering, he told me.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，我们正非常接近那种将防止大量患者痛苦的大规模、个性化医疗。

sentences.en: Across the country and even around the world, pain research has been galvanized by a new awareness, which in turn is leading to new initiatives and investments.
sentences.zh: 在全国乃至全世界，疼痛研究受到了新意识的激发，这反过来又带来新的倡议和投资。

sentences.en: The European Pain Federation has already published a proposal to improve the current and future management of chronic pain in Europe.
sentences.zh: 欧洲疼痛联盟已经发布了一项提案，旨在改善欧洲当前和未来的慢性疼痛管理。

sentences.en: And in 2024, Britain announced an ongoing research consortium that aims to break through the complexity of pain and find new treatments for a wide spectrum of chronic conditions.
sentences.zh: 2024年，英国宣布了一项正在进行的研究所联合体，旨在突破疼痛的复杂性，为广泛的慢性病情寻找新的治疗方法。

sentences.en: It's been a real shift, Motzkin added.
sentences.zh: 莫茨金补充说，这是一个真正的转变。

sentences.en: I'm profoundly optimistic about the future of chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 我对慢性疼痛的未来深感乐观。

sentences.en: As for me, a little more than a year after my arms went berserk, they started to get better.
sentences.zh: 至于我，在我的手臂抓狂一年多后，它们开始好转了。

sentences.en: Gradually, at first, and then more quickly.
sentences.zh: 起初是逐渐地，然后变得更快。

sentences.en: I went from not being able to drive at all to being able to make short local trips to going all the way across the bridge into San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我从完全不能开车，到能够进行本地短途旅行，再到一路穿过大桥进入旧金山。

sentences.en: But just as no one could figure out what caused the pain, no one could explain why it got better.
sentences.zh: 但就像没有人能弄清楚是什么引起了疼痛一样，也没有人能解释它为什么会好转。

sentences.en: A physical therapist told me that nerves heal slowly, so time, I guess.
sentences.zh: 一个物理治疗师告诉我神经愈合得很慢，所以我想只能靠时间了。

sentences.en: Regardless, I'm now again able to chop vegetables and lift a pot of water onto the stove and use my laptop to write.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我现在又可以切菜、把一锅水端到炉子上以及用笔记本电脑写作了。

sentences.en: Even so, my arms still hurt every day and limit what I can do.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，我的胳膊每天仍然会痛，并且限制了我的活动能力。

sentences.en: In other words, while I'm thankful for my luck and deeply relieved to be able to work again, it's hard not to wish for a real fix, one in which I magically returned to the body
sentences.zh: 换句话说，虽然我很感激自己的运气，也为能够重新工作感到由衷的欣慰，但还是很难不渴望一个真正的解决方案，一个能让我神奇地回到那个身体的方案

sentences.en: that, for years, simply worked.
sentences.zh: 那个多年来一直运转正常的身体。

sentences.en: A body that I don't constantly have to think about.
sentences.zh: 一个我不用时刻去挂念的身体。

sentences.en: And though the prospect of a new era of pain treatment has me hopeful, it's also still excruciatingly out of reach.
sentences.zh: 虽然疼痛治疗新时代的前景让我看到了希望，但它目前依然遥不可及。

sentences.en: For me, and for everyone else who has lost months or years or decades of their life to pain,
sentences.zh: 对我而言，以及对所有因为疼痛而失去了生命中数月、数年甚至数十年的人来说

sentences.en: the future can't come soon enough.
sentences.zh: 未来真的可以说是越快到来越好。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目中，我们将为假期招待客人做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的妙招。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种对光线极度敏感的深度睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到不省人事才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》App或你喜欢的任何播客平台上搜索《Wirecutter秀》。
